title: Winter Has a Joy for Me
description: Winter Has a Joy for Me in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 83, “I will praise the Lord at all times”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Win-ter has a joy for me, While the Sa-vior's charms I read, Low-ly, meek, from blem-ish free, In the snow drop's pen-sive head.

lines: Winter has a joy for me,
While the Savior's charms I read,
Seems to speak his dying groans!
'Tis his sun that lights and warms,
His the air that cools the earth.
What, has autumn left to say
Yes, the beams of milder day
Tell me of his smiling face.
While the sun makes haste to rise,
On the blushes of the skies.
Shows an emblem of his grace,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
